title: Data Analytics & Automation Specialist
desc: Hours: Full-Time – 35 Hours Work Location: 30-30 Thomson Avenue, LIC, NY 11101 The Technology and Innovation Division (T&I) within the New York City Department of Design and Construction (DDC) seeks to hire a skilled, data-driven Data Analytics & Automation Specialist. DDC is the City’s primary capital construction agency, responsible for delivering safe, sustainable, and innovative public buildings and infrastructure across the five boroughs. Partnering with client agencies, design professionals, and the construction industry, DDC manages a broad portfolio of projects from firehouses, libraries, and community centers to roadways, sewers, and resiliency initiatives helping to shape a more equitable, efficient, and resilient city. Through its commitment to design excellence, technological modernization, and public service, DDC ensures that critical civic projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest standards of quality. The Technology and Innovation (T&I) Division serves as DDC’s centralized Information, Technology, and Telecom operation, organized into four core units: Network, Infrastructure and Security; Service Delivery; Application Development, and Administrative Analytics. Together, these units provide the hardware, software, enterprise applications, and data ecosystem that support the agency’s daily operations. In addition to maintaining core systems, the division leads strategic modernization efforts aimed at improving efficiency, strengthening security, and advancing programmatic excellence across the agency. Reporting directly to the Director of Administrative Analytics, the Data Analytics & Automation Specialist will blend business intelligence and reporting with hands-on data engineering and automation. The selected candidate will build the dashboards leadership relies on and the automated pipelines that feed them across HR, budget, contracting, procurement, and other administrative functions. The ideal candidate will combine strong technical skills in business intelligence, SQL, Python, and automation with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and will be comfortable working directly with non-technical users to gather requirements, conceptualize business challenges, and deliver practical solutions. title: Strategy Analyst
desc: Job Summary The Strategy Analyst supports executive and health system leadership across the enterprise by translating complex internal, market, and industry datasets into actionable strategic insights. Operating within the Business Development department, this role focuses on evaluating market share dynamics, optimizing ambulatory and inpatient access points, supporting service line planning, and supporting enterprise capacity planning. The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative modeling skills with healthcare domain fluency to inform capital allocation, network expansion, and long-term strategic planning. Essential Functions Market Share & Competitive Intelligence: Analyze external claims, state inpatient/outpatient discharge databases, and demographic data to evaluate market share trends, competitor positioning, migration patterns, and whitespace opportunities across primary and secondary service areas. Service Line Analytics: Partner with service line executives and physician leaders to assess clinical program performance, volume trajectories, payer mix shifts, contribution margins, and downstream referral patterns. Access Point & Network Optimization: Conduct geospatial and catchment area analyses to evaluate ambulatory footprint performance, site-of-care shifts, clinic utilization, and optimal locations for new facilities or service expansions. Capacity Planning & Demand Forecasting: Build quantitative models to project inpatient bed demand, procedural room utilization, and ambulatory capacity constraints based on population health trends, clinical acuity, and operational throughput. Executive Decision Support: Synthesize multi-source findings into clear, executive-ready presentations and business cases that guide strategic planning, partnership evaluations, and capital investments. ***Hybrid in Franklin, TN strongly preferred. Fully remote considered for standout candidates with exceptional experience*** Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Economics, Data Science, Finance, Statistics, Public Health, or a related quantitative field required; Master’s degree (MHA, MPH, MBA, or MS in Analytics) is strongly preferred. Experience: Minimum of 2–4 years of experience in healthcare strategy, management consulting, decision support, or quantitative analytics. Direct experience working within a hospital, multi-hospital health system, payer, or healthcare consulting environment strongly preferred. Technical Background: Experience working with large-scale healthcare datasets (e.g., Epic/Cerner EHR extracts, Cost Accounting/Decision Support systems, state/all-payer claims data, CMS datasets, or syndicated market intelligence platforms such as Sg2, Advisory Board, or Claritas). Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) Healthcare Domain Knowledge: Understanding of hospital and ambulatory operations, healthcare reimbursement models, service line economics (e.g., DRGs, APCs, RVUs), and competitive market dynamics. Analytical & Data Visualization Skills: Proficiency in Excel for complex data analysis and financial/volume modeling; demonstrated ability to build intuitive visuals in Tableau, Power BI, or Excel. Strategic Communication: Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint to design clean, structured, executive-ready slide decks. Ability to distill technical analyses into concise business narratives for executives, clinical leaders, and other non-technical stakeholders. Project Management & Collaboration: Self-directed with strong organizational skills to manage multiple competing strategic initiatives simultaneously while maintaining rigorous attention to analytical accuracy.

title: Data Scientist, Integrity
desc:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

 - Trace where signals, review decisions, or enforcement actions break down. Work with partners to close gaps and build reusable datasets, analyses, and investigation tools.



IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - You use AI tools to investigate large, messy datasets, test hypotheses quickly, and automate recurring analyses. You’re fluent in SQL and Python and can verify AI-generated queries, code, and conclusions against the underlying data.

 - You have strong statistical judgment and experience with experimentation, causal inference, or observational analysis. You can reason from incomplete or biased labels and explain how uncertainty affects a decision.

 - You take ownership of open-ended problems, from deciding what to measure through recommending an action and checking whether it worked.

 - You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners and can explain the tradeoffs behind a recommendation.

 - Experience in integrity, trust and safety, fraud or risk analytics, security analytics, or applied ML evaluation is helpful. Experience evaluating detection systems, human review, or LLM-based classifiers is a plus.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.
